title: A stronger electric field
hook: Change electric-field magnitude and predict electric-force magnitude.
misconception: electric-force magnitude stays fixed when electric-field magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply F = abs(q)E to compare electric-force magnitude when electric-field magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed test-charge magnitude, F = abs(q)E. When electric-field magnitude doubles, electric-force magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F = abs(q)E; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed test-charge magnitude, with a nonzero initial result. If electric-field magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-force magnitude?
recall.why: Apply F = abs(q)E under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
